Mercedes-AMG’s GT SUV Is Coming for the Porsche Cayenne Electric - Rendering
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
Mercedes has plenty of things on its plate these days, as it is preparing to update several models. Not only that, but its performance-oriented division based in Affalterbach is also about to expand its portfolio.
You do know what we are talking about, don’t you? That’s right, the upcoming Mercedes- AMG SUV , which does not yet have an official name. Well, it likely does, we just do not know it, as the automaker hasn’t released that many details about it. It is simply known as the GT SUV so far for a very good reason: it builds on the same platform as the all-new GT 4-Door Coupe . You know, the electric model that definitely won’t win any beauty pageants.
That’s quite a surprising move, to say the least, because while most gearheads and their pets can agree that the new-gen Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe is anything but pretty, yet that hasn’t stopped the company from giving it a high-riding alternative. We have seen the upcoming machine on a few occasions, mostly with camouflage wrapped around its entire exterior, but the rendering crowd has also done a great job, for the most part, at imagining what it looks like beneath the fake skin.
It was at the end of last week that we have seen a quite realistic take on it , and that one came from @sugardesign_1 on Instagram. More recently, the Mercedes-AMG GT SUV has been imagined yet again, and the computer generated images that you can see in the photo gallery here came from @kelsonik. This pixel master’s work is usually on the very realistic side of things, so what you see here is basically what you will get when the model finally goes official, and the unveiling date is right around the corner in case you forgot.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Mercedes itself recently announced that this model is due just shortly. It will be officially shown to the world this week, and the date to save is October 17, 2026. That’s this Saturday, in case you were wondering. Codenamed the X591, the Mercedes-AMG GT SUV looks very similar to its low-riding sibling. It features an almost-identical front fascia, complete with the familiar-looking star-studded headlights, linked together in the middle by a thin light strip.
Further down, it will have a familiar Panamericana grille with vertical slats, decorated in the middle by the three-pointed star logo. The front bumper is home to a pair of vertical vents, and to an air intake on the lower part. Further back, it features similar lines to the new Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe on the sides, as well as flush door handles, but the profile does not have anything else in common with it.
That’s because the doors and side windows are much taller here, to no one’s surprise, and there are also some discreet roof rails on deck. The rear fascia is home to the same quirky lighting signature, as well as the trim surrounding it, and the one in the middle of the tailgate. The rear bumper is an adaptation of the one equipping the GT 4-Door Coupe. The diffuser is a bit less aggressive on this crossover, and the wheels are similar in these renderings signed by the quoted pixel master.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Mercedes-AMG’s GT SUV is presented here in yellow, and it is contrasted by the black elements. These include the roof, roof rails, side window surrounds, rear diffuser, the outer edges of the roof-mounted spoiler, the grille, and the wheels, among others. The rendering artist has done a great job at sketching out this upcoming model, because as we already told you, the CGI-infused design is realistic.
Look for the same powertrain family as the new Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, with a tri-motor setup powering the crossover in the range-topping flavor. The low-riding model has 1,153 hp (860 kW/1,169 ps) to play with and 1,475 lb-ft (2,000 Nm) of torque in total in the top-of-the-line grade, taking 2.1 seconds from 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) with the 1-foot rollout, or 2.4 seconds without it. Flat-out, it will do 186 mph (300 kph), and it has a 432-mile (696 km) range with the 106 kWh battery pack fully charged.
We expect similar performance from the upcoming Mercedes-AMG GT SUV , though this model should be a tiny bit slower. A dual-motor setup is likely on the cards, too, offering 805 hp (600 kW/816 ps) and 1,328 pound-feet (1,800 Nm) of torque. Additional highlights will likely include rear-wheel steering, air suspension, semi-active roll stabilization, and a few other things.
With the official unveiling date just a few days away, we do not have to wait that long to learn the secrets of this model, which will take on the likes of the Porsche Cayenne Electric, including its name. But if you held the reins of Mercedes, what would you name the electric super crossover? To be honest, the GT SUV is not a bad name at all, though it’s not exactly the most inspiring either.
